what: REFUTED EXEMPLAR for II.19 (the convergent-inference test, entered as the 14th amendment): two channels are offered as independent support for a posited rental status, but both trace to the same upstream booking feed — a wire copy wearing convergence's vocabulary. II.2 can only say 'no giver'; II.19 names the actual defect: the channels share a derivation, so the claim is citogenesis, not an etak.

etak.posited_entity: STR availability status for property #48213 (a status-at-this-moment bearing, per the as-of snapshot)

channels.signal: listing carries an 'available' state on the property's own booking feed
channels.derivation: scheduled scrape of the property's booking feed
channels.independence_basis: claimed: different scraper binary than scraper-B; no shared code path

channels.signal: the same 'available' state is observed again
channels.derivation: second pipeline, but pointed at the same upstream booking feed
channels.independence_basis: FAILS II.19 disjoint derivation: shares the upstream feed with scraper-A; B is a wire copy of A's source, not an independent channel. A downstream derivation is not a second channel.

etak.predicted_effect: if the posited status is real, each independently-derived channel should observe it

fit_improvement.note: also fails the baseline discipline: two copies of the same feed cannot raise the joint fit above one — the without-posit model already explains both channels
